stories.headline: Murasu cyclone disrupts flight services at Vijayawada airport
stories.title: Murasu cyclone disrupts flight services at Vijayawada airport
stories.summary: IndiGo cancels eight flights scheduled for November 3
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Vijayawada: Cyclone Murasu has disrupted flight operations at Vijayawada International Airport at Gannavaram, with several services cancelled on Monday and Tuesday (November 3), causing inconvenience to passengers travelling to various destinations.
IndiGo has cancelled eight flight operations scheduled for Tuesday (November 3) to and from Vijayawada as a precautionary measure in view of the cyclone.

According to information shared by the Airport officials, the cancellations include seven domestic services and one international flight, affecting connectivity with Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai, Kadapa and Singapore.

Among the cancelled morning services are the Delhi-Vijayawada-Delhi flight (6E 6446/6447), scheduled to arrive at 7.25 am and depart at 7.55 am, and the Bengaluru-Vijayawada-Bengaluru service (6E 7203/7204), scheduled between 7.30 am and 7.55 am.
The Hyderabad service (6E 2572/2573), scheduled to arrive at 8.15 am and depart at 8.45 am, and the Chennai flight (6E 7303/7304), scheduled between 8.30 am and 9 am, have also been cancelled.
The international Singapore service (6E 1030/1029), scheduled to arrive at 7.55 am and depart at 9.40 am, has also been called off.
The cancellations will continue through the afternoon and evening.

The Hyderabad service (6E 6326/6327), scheduled between 1.15 pm and 1.45 pm, the Kadapa-Vijayawada-Kadapa flight (6E 7711/7712), scheduled between 2.30 pm and 2.50 pm, and the evening Bengaluru service (6E 7223/7224), scheduled to arrive at 5.25 pm and depart at 5.45 pm, have also been cancelled.
The flight disruptions have affected passengers travelling for business, official work, education, medical treatment and onward domestic and international connections.
Passengers have been advised to check their flight status with the respective airlines before leaving for the airport and contact airline authorities regarding rescheduling and refunds.
Normal flight operations will depend on improvement in weather conditions and the assessment of the aviation authorities.

stories.headline: Cyclone Murasu makes landfall, Andhra on alert as storm unleashes 120 kmph winds
stories.title: Cyclone Murasu makes landfall, Andhra on alert as storm unleashes 120 kmph winds
stories.summary: Cyclone Murasu makes landfall, Andhra on alert as storm unleashes 120 kmph winds
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Cyclone Murasu began making landfall near Ongole with heavy rain and gale-force winds.
The storm prompted flight cancellations, surge warnings and large-scale restoration preparations.

Severe cyclonic storm Murasu began its landfall process near Ongole in Andhra Pradesh's Prakasam district around 1 am on Tuesday, bringing heavy rainfall and gale-force winds of up to 110 kmph, with gusts reaching 120 kmph, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said.
In its bulletin at 1.30 am, the IMD said the cyclone was centred over the west-central Bay of Bengal, around 40 km southeast of Ongole, 60 km northeast of Kavali and 70 km south of Bapatla.
The forward sector of the cyclone's wall cloud had started entering the coast, with the landfall process expected to continue through the early hours.
The IMD warned that gale-force winds of 110 kmph, gusting up to 120 kmph, were likely along and off the South Andhra Pradesh coast until morning.
Heavy rainfall was also forecast across South Coastal Andhra Pradesh over the next 12 hours.
A storm surge of 1-1.5 metres above the astronomical tide was likely to inundate low-lying areas until Wednesday morning.
Bapatla, Krishna and Prakasam districts were expected to witness the maximum impact of the surge.
At least 19 domestic flights across Vijayawada, Tirupati and Visakhapatnam airports were cancelled on Monday as the cyclone approached the Andhra Pradesh coast.
Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu has directed officials to remain on high alert and take all necessary precautionary measures to prevent loss of life and property.

During a review meeting on Monday, Naidu said the impact of Murasu was likely to be less severe than Cyclone Arnab but stressed the need for effective preparedness as moderate to heavy rainfall was expected across South Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema districts.

stories.headline: Maharashtra sets up drought mitigation panel, approves ₹291.91 crore relief for flood-hit farmers
stories.title: Maharashtra sets up drought mitigation panel, approves ₹291.91 crore relief for flood-hit farmers
stories.summary: The measures follow deficient rainfall in parts of Maharashtra during 2026, prompting the government to declare drought in talukas identified under the Kharif season’s Trigger-1 assessment
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Maharashtra government on Monday (November 1, 2026) announced measures to address drought and flood-related agricultural distress across the State, constituting a high-level committee headed by the Chief Minister to oversee soil and water conservation projects in drought-affected areas and approving ₹291.91 crore in financial assistance for farmers affected by heavy rainfall and flooding between June and August 2026.

Soil and Water Conservation Minister Sanjay Rathod said the committee would monitor conservation projects undertaken through non-governmental organisations, including Paani Foundation and Chandra Foundation, as part of the state’s drought mitigation efforts.
The government has also decided to revive Paani Foundation’s Water Cup competition to encourage community participation in water conservation.
The measures follow deficient rainfall in parts of Maharashtra during 2026, prompting the government to declare drought in talukas identified under the Kharif season’s Trigger-1 assessment.

According to a government resolution issued on November 2, all Deputy Chief Ministers will serve as co-chairpersons of the high-level committee, which will include ministers from departments such as agriculture, water resources, rural development and employment guarantee.
A separate executive committee, chaired by the Principal Secretary of the Water Resources Department, will coordinate implementation and meet at least once a month.
Progress will be monitored using geographical information systems (GIS), satellite imagery, mobile-based monitoring systems and online dashboards.

Meanwhile, Relief and Rehabilitation Minister Makarand Jadhav Patil announced that the government had sanctioned ₹262.70 crore for crop damage affecting 3,09,289 farmers across six revenue divisions, including Pune, Nagpur, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Amravati, Konkan and Nashik.
An additional ₹29.21 crore has been approved for damage to agricultural land covering 7,675.40 hectares belonging to 34,984 farmers.
The assistance will cover eligible restoration work, including the removal of sand, silt and salt deposits caused by flooding.

Crop damage compensation will be transferred directly to eligible farmers’ bank accounts, while small and marginal landowners will receive assistance for damaged agricultural land up to a maximum of two hectares, in accordance with prescribed norms.
The government has also directed district collectors to ensure that banks do not divert disaster relief payments towards loan repayments or other recoveries.

stories.headline: Army organises first-ever Gujjar and Bakarwal outreach programme in Wadder, Handwara
stories.title: Army organises first-ever Gujjar and Bakarwal outreach programme in Wadder, Handwara
stories.summary: Handwara, Nov 2: In a significant initiative aimed at promoting community engagement and strengthening ties with local residents, a Rashtriya Rifles unit organised a special outreach programme for the Gujjar and Bakarwal communities in the Wadder Rajwar area of Handwara for the first time. The programme witnessed enthusiastic participation from members of the local community and featured a series of cultural, recreational and sports activities designed to encourage community bonding and celebrate the rich cultural heritage of the Gujjar and Bakarwal communities. Various activities, including a Gojri singing competition, tug of war, jalebi jump, lemon race and sack race, were organised as part of the programme. These activities provided an opportunity for local residents, particularly youth and children, to showcase their talent and participate in a spirit of enthusiasm and camaraderie. A free medical camp was also organised during the event, providing medical assistance to members of the Gujjar and Bakarwal communities. Locals warmly appreciated the initiative taken by the Indian Army, describing it as a meaningful effort to reach out to the community and promote mutual understanding and goodwill. They also expressed gratitude to 21 Rashtriya Rifles for organising the programme and requested the Army to make such outreach activities an annual feature in Wadder Rajwar. The programme concluded with appreciation from community members, who termed the initiative a positive step towards strengthening the bond between the Indian Army and the local population.

stories.headline: Ram Madhav arriving on day-long visit to Jammu today
stories.title: Ram Madhav arriving on day-long visit to Jammu today
stories.summary: Jammu, Nov 2: Amid ongoing political churning in J&K on different accounts, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national vice president Ram Madhav is arriving in Jammu on a day-long visit tomorrow, November 3, 2026. The visit, which, according to the party, is aimed at holding only organisational meetings and deflating opposition-manufactured SIR controversy, has assumed significance, or more appropriately created flutter in the political corridors of J&K. In fact, political spins are being measured against his (Madhav’s) impressive past track-record vis-a-vis handling such politically tricky situations and carving “brighter opportunities” out of crisis or turbulence for the party as its (BJP's) point-man in J&K. J&K remembers him (Madhav) as the man, who made possible what used to be perceived as “impossible” –stitching BJP-PDP coalition to govern J&K in 2015 through “Agenda of Alliance” formulated along with Haseeb Drabu, former Finance Minister and the then senior PDP leader. But the J&K BJP unit dismisses all these angles as “rumour-mongering.” “He (Madhav) will be coming tomorrow morning. Initially there will be some party meetings. Later, he will be addressing media at 1 pm at BJP headquarter, Trikuta Nagar, Jammu,” shared J&K BJP chief spokesperson Sunil Sethi, while responding to Greater Kashmir queries about the central leader’s visit, his itinerary and major engagements. With regard to a question about the speculations linking Madhav’s visit to present spell of political upheaval in the UT amid chinks in National Conference's armour given open rebellion by its (NC's) veterans - post recent J&K cabinet expansion, Sethi dismissed such “spins” as “only conjectures.” “That is purely speculative. Presently there is no such effort. He is coming for the organisational meeting(s) followed by a press conference and addressing the concerns and clear deliberate confusion being created on Special Intensive Revision (SIR) (amid opposition propaganda). On SIR, the press conferences (by the party) are being held across the country – in different states and Union Territories (UTs). So that is all, one central leader is coming along with the state team,” Sethi said. “BJP national vice president is coming for that purpose. Rest is speculative that he is coming to form the government. He cannot comment upon that. There is no such thing, officially with us. Tomorrow’s visit is not related to anything like government formation or some political equations. There is nothing like that. It is a routine SIR-related press conference and organisational activities,” the J&K BJP chief spokesperson asserted. Will NC rebellion or evolving scenario post cabinet expansion be part of deliberations during J&K BJP organisational meetings with Madhav? “See, we are keenly watching what is happening in the National Conference. Presently there is no decision of making any move in this direction by the BJP. Even otherwise I don’t think so. These types of things will never be discussed in the organisational meetings. So there’s no need to see or read more than that (with regard to Madhav’s visit),” Sethi maintains. Nevertheless, it is not just BJP keenly watching developments unfolding in the NC, all political beings, including analysts in J&K or outside, are also earnestly following its (BJP’s) each and every move. Madhav was the party’s election in-charge for the 2024 J&K assembly polls. He was appointed national vice president earlier this year as part of the organisational team under party president Nitin Nabin. Interestingly, BJP national vice president’s Jammu visit will coincide with another significant political development unfolding in Srinagar on November 3, 2026 – the resignation of Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi - NC MP from Srinagar parliamentary constituency both from Lok Sabha as well as from party (NC). Just a coincidence, probably!
